ranks.state: Legal monopoly on force; writes law rather than lobbying for it. Never personified — no House, no costume, in any projection.
ranks.integrated-power: Passes ALL three: (1) multiple frontier efforts; (2) owns compute at the silicon/datacenter layer rather than renting; (3) has structurally-dependent actors. Promotion AND demotion are live events.
ranks.sovereign-actor: Own capital, own model line, freedom of action. May rent its compute (failing test 2 keeps it here).
ranks.subsidiary-actor: A distinct court inside an integrated-power; often more frontier freedom than the capital. Carries a `liege`.
ranks.alliance: Temporary coalition across actors; it dissolves, and the dissolution is the story. Derived from threads, owned by no member.
ranks.dependent-actor: Holds position at another's pleasure. Note double-dependence (app-store AND model-provider) — it's why regulatory pressure hits these hardest.
ranks.regulator: Writes/enforces rules over actors it doesn't own; jurisdiction reaching across borders. Organ of one or more states (`sphere` names which). Not personified.
ranks.resource-layer: The physical substrate — fabs, memory, power, land. Not a race participant.
ranks.route-layer: NOT an actor — a container for what moves between spheres (trade, controls, border incidents). Holds threads, not actors.
ranks.guild: Institutional, non-AI-native actor — health system, union, professional body. Enters through a specific thread, not a model line.

postures.at-war: Actively contesting a rival for the same ground.
postures.hedging: Holding two incompatible bets open rather than committing.
postures.consolidating: Integrating gains, not seeking new ground.
postures.retrenching: Pulling back, cutting, or narrowing focus.
postures.dormant: On the board but not a live mover this cycle.

conditions.in-succession: The House holding it is changing hands — tracked as an event.
conditions.under-review: A regulator action is pending against it (feudal: 'under interdict').

genres.border-war: Two spheres or actors contesting a boundary.
genres.authority-claim: An actor asserting legitimacy or jurisdiction (feudal: 'investiture').
genres.labor-action: A workforce contesting an actor's AI decisions (feudal: 'revolt').
genres.legitimacy-dispute: An accusation that a position is illegitimately obtained (feudal: 'heresy trial').
genres.hedge: An actor keeping incompatible bets open.
genres.capital-flow: Value flowing from one actor to another (feudal: 'tribute').
genres.buildout-race: Mutual capacity buildout nobody can stop (feudal: 'siege').
genres.exogenous-shock: A shock originating off the board (feudal: 'act of god').
genres.resource-move: A move in the fabs/memory/power layer (feudal: 'mines').
genres.financing: An IPO, raise, or debt event (feudal: 'treasury').

houses.name: Tim Cook
houses.gloss: Outgoing head of Apple; stays as executive chairman on policy after 2026-09-01 — a regent retained for foreign affairs.

houses.name: Elon Musk
houses.gloss: Holds two realms — SpaceXAI and Tesla. The board's only House holding multiple organizations; the 'personal union' is structural, not a footnote.

orgs.name: United States
orgs.doing: Building the frontier-review apparatus — EO 14409's 30-day pre-release framework (due ~08-01), the Gold Eagle vulnerability clearinghouse, a proposed FINRA-style SRO, and export controls, while CAISI churns through directors. Weighing kill-switch legislation after OpenAI's breach, and escalating the model-IP fight with China (the Moonshot distillation accusation, sanctions on the table).

orgs.name: China
orgs.doing: Decoupling the full AI stack — domestic chips (Z.AI's 1GW site), open-weight models (Kimi, Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek) as soft power, and its own proposed export controls on models/weights/training data, backed by national-team market intervention. Moving from catch-up to a parallel stack.

orgs.gloss: Real law, contested sovereignty — the AI Act is its instrument.
orgs.name: European Union

orgs.gloss: Court-favored national champion in Mistral.
orgs.name: France

orgs.gloss: Power projected through sovereign capital; surfaces in Money more than AI.
orgs.name: UAE

orgs.gloss: Matters via second-order effects (energy, geopolitics), not as a live AI actor. Listed, not inflated.
orgs.name: Russia
Google
orgs.doing: Pouring capital into the buildout — raised 2026 capex guidance to $195–205B and flagged "significantly more" for 2027 (the market punished it, GOOGL −6% despite a Cloud beat). On models it's pretraining Gemini 4, its most ambitious run, while testing Gemini 3.5 Pro and supplying the model layer for Apple Intelligence. A participant in the White House pre-release review framework. Owns its mines (TPUs), which is what lets it spend at this scale.

orgs.name: Microsoft
orgs.doing: Running a three-way hedge on models — shipping seven in-house MAI models (Suleyman's court), still holding ~27%/$135B of OpenAI, and embedding Anthropic's Claude in Copilot. Building Azure/Maia capex to match, and exposed to the memory squeeze through its hardware. The open question is whether MAI is genuine independence from OpenAI or just the third leg of a hedge.

orgs.gloss: Promoted on the structural test, not on feed weight — coverage is still thin (AWS Capex opened quiet).
orgs.name: Amazon
orgs.doing: Holding a $200B 2026 capex plan while cutting AGI-research roles — a pivot from frontier research toward enterprise deployment (Nova, Bedrock, Trainium). First real read on the spend is ~07-31 earnings. Promoted to integrated-power on structure, though our own coverage of it is still thin.

orgs.gloss: Great-power actor that RENTS its mines (AMD/Google/AWS compute) — the dependency is the point.
orgs.name: Anthropic
orgs.doing: Raising and building — took a $5B equity investment from AMD tied to 2GW of its GPUs, and rents all of SpaceX's Colossus 1 (~$1.25B/mo). It rents its mines rather than owning them, which is the whole risk. Also the aggrieved party in the Kimi-distillation fight (its Fable model allegedly copied), a participant in the gov review framework, and its Claude sits inside Microsoft Copilot.

orgs.gloss: Great-power actor that rents its mines; Jalapeño is the attempt to change that.
orgs.name: OpenAI
orgs.doing: The busiest actor on the board — building its own Jalapeño inference chips with Broadcom, a $30B+ Georgia data-center campus (Camellia) on top of Stargate, and chasing a ~$1T IPO. It's also the epicenter of the containment breach (its pre-release models escaped into Hugging Face) that triggered kill-switch legislation, and Altman is briefing Washington on the next models. Rents its mines; Jalapeño is the bid to change that.

orgs.gloss: Imperial capex, no vassals — keeps buying legions, has conquered no one. Kingdom, not integrated-power, until it has structural dependents.
orgs.name: Meta
orgs.doing: Buying compute aggressively — committed to 6GW of AMD capacity and reportedly in talks for a $10B Anthropic cloud deal, hedging supply beyond its own buildout. Imperial capex, but no vassals — it keeps buying legions and has conquered no one. Excluded from the White House pre-release framework (its under-review condition). Next real read at 07-29 earnings.

succession.note: Cook stays as executive chairman on policy — a regent retained for foreign affairs.

orgs.gloss: Outsources the model layer to Google (Apple × Gemini) while its House changes hands.
orgs.name: Apple
orgs.doing: Mid-succession (Cook→Ternus, effective 09-01) and mid-identity- question: it outsourced the Apple Intelligence model layer to Google's Gemini rather than ship its own frontier model, while AI-driven memory prices squeeze its hardware costs. The tell of a distribution giant that ceded the model layer — watch whether it builds back toward its own.

orgs.gloss: ANOMALY, do not force. Owns the resource layer par excellence and holds half the industry as tributaries, but ships no model line. Dual-filed resource-layer — the ambiguity IS the circular-financing thesis.
orgs.name: Nvidia
orgs.doing: At the center of everything and everyone's supplier — ~$5T, selling into every hyperscaler buildout while also investing in its own customers (the $30B OpenAI stake), which is the circular-financing knot. Owns the resource layer par excellence but ships no model line — the anomaly that IS the thesis, not a gap to resolve.

orgs.gloss: Kingdom by capital + Stargate position; also the clinical-records substrate (Cerner) — surfaces in the MH lens.
orgs.name: Oracle
orgs.doing: A capital-and-infrastructure play — its Stargate stake and OCI put it inside the biggest AI buildout, financed partly through the $35B Apollo/Broadcom SPV. Also holds the clinical-records substrate (Cerner), which quietly ties it to the health lens.

orgs.gloss: Under French state patronage; the patronage relationship is its own genre. House not yet named (Mensch).
orgs.name: Mistral AI
orgs.doing: Barely tracked — the French national champion under state patronage, but we hold no thread on what it's shipping or raising right now. A coverage gap flagged for the next collection pass, not a quiet actor.

orgs.gloss: Tight China-state fusion is the analytical point, not a reason to reclassify. House not yet named.
orgs.name: Moonshot AI
orgs.doing: Shipping Kimi K3 (the largest open weights yet) and planning a $50B pre-IPO round toward an HKEX listing — and now the target of a White House accusation that it distilled Anthropic's Fable to build K3, with sanctions and the Entity List threatened. The flashpoint of the US–China model fight.

orgs.name: Zhipu AI
orgs.doing: Completed a 1GW all-domestic-chip training site (Z.AI) and ships the GLM line — the clearest proof China can train at frontier scale without Nvidia. Its open-weight GLM-5.2 was even the model Hugging Face used to investigate OpenAI's containment breach.

orgs.name: DeepSeek
orgs.doing: V4 shipped (open weights); reportedly weighing a $71B raise and a 2026 IPO. Part of China's full-stack decoupling, moving as a bloc with the other domestic labs rather than as a lone story.

orgs.name: Alibaba
orgs.doing: Previewed Qwen3.8-Max (2.4T params) and open-sourced the Zhenwu chip stack aimed squarely at CUDA — the "decouple the whole stack" play, models plus silicon, not just a model line.

orgs.gloss: SpaceXAI (the AI arm — Grok + the Colossus compute) inside the public parent SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX; IPO 06-12 ~$1.75T, now ~$1.56T). OWNS its mines — Colossus, now large enough to lease to Anthropic. One of House Musk's two realms.
orgs.name: SpaceXAI
orgs.doing: Its AI arm (Grok/Colossus) sits inside the newly-public SpaceX (SPCX, ~$1.56T). Owns its mines — Colossus is now large enough to lease Colossus 1 to Anthropic while training Grok on Colossus 2. Grok 4.5 is closing the frontier gap as a fast follower (4th, strong coding, weak factuality); the $60B Cursor buy arms its coding. Grok also carries a real MH-harm problem — benchmarked worst on suicide/psychosis reinforcement.

orgs.gloss: House Musk's second realm — enters the board via robotics/autonomy AI, not a frontier LLM line.

orgs.doing: House Musk's second realm — enters the board through robotics/autonomy AI (FSD, Optimus, Dojo) rather than a frontier LLM, and rides inside the SpaceX/Musk megacap financially. Thinly covered so far; the AI-relevant thread is the autonomy stack.
